name: essay perfect
question: Explain why a recursive function needs a base case.

rubric.point: recursion means the function calls itself
the base case stops the recursion
without it the calls never end and the stack overflows

model_answer: A recursive function calls itself, so it needs a base case that stops the calls. Without one it keeps calling itself until the stack memory runs out, a stack overflow.
source: Every recursive function needs a base case that stops the recursion
answer: Recursion is when a function calls itself again and again. The base case is the condition where it stops calling itself and returns. If there is no base case the calls never end, so the program runs out of stack memory and crashes with a stack overflow.

answer: The base case is what makes the function stop calling itself.

name: ceiling full
question: Explain why a price ceiling set below equilibrium causes a shortage.

rubric.point: a price ceiling is a legal maximum price
at the low price, quantity demanded is more than quantity supplied
the gap between them is a shortage

model_answer: A price ceiling is a legal maximum price. Set below equilibrium, it keeps the price low, so people want to buy more than sellers want to supply, and the gap is a shortage.
source: A price ceiling is a legal maximum price; when set below equilibrium it causes a shortage.
answer: A price ceiling is the highest price the law allows. If it is below equilibrium, the price is so low that buyers want more of the good than sellers are willing to supply. That missing amount is the shortage.

name: ceiling thin
answer: Because the price is too low there is a shortage.

name: ceiling confused
answer: A price ceiling is a minimum price like the minimum wage, so sellers make too much and there is a surplus.

name: array list full
question: Explain how an array and a linked list differ.

rubric.point: an array stores elements in contiguous memory
an array reads any element by index in constant time
a linked list stores nodes that point to the next node
inserting into a linked list is cheap but finding the nth element means walking the list

model_answer: An array keeps its elements side by side in memory, so any element is read in constant time by its index. A linked list keeps nodes that point to the next one, so inserting is cheap but reaching the nth element means walking the list.
source: An array stores elements of the same type in contiguous memory, so any element can be read in constant time by its index.
answer: An array keeps all its elements next to each other in memory, so you can jump straight to any element by its index in constant time. A linked list is made of nodes where each node points to the next one. Adding a node is cheap, but to find the 5th element you have to walk through the list from the start.

name: array list half
answer: An array stores its elements next to each other in memory.
